answer: In this PoA design, identity verification binds each node to a Wesolowski VDF requiring a continuous chain of modular squarings, with every result needed before the next operation. An attacker can start separate chains for walnut, signal, and quartz identities, but GPUs cannot parallelize the dependency chain or reduce its per-instance latency; they only add hardware and energy costs. This strict elapsed-time bottleneck makes large-scale Sybil cloning expensive.
